original_value: Recently Mobile technology is considered an effective way to improve students' skills such as positive thinking, collaborative, communication, as well as it is considered the main part of major innovation in many e-learning research areas. As a result of the 21<sup>st.</sup> century requirements, skills were developed to address the rising needs in higher education which causes a shifting paradigm from the traditional methods of teaching to M-learning. In this research, we discuss the effect of using Mobile learning techniques to improve learning outcomes in Higher Education. We have implemented a web-based survey through two questionnaires. The questionnaires were distributed among 200 students in the second and third levels in the computer science department at both Community College and College of Arts and Science. This research explores a study on e-learning using mobile technology to identify students’ perceptions in the acceptance of mobile techniques and recognize the quality of mobile services for academic and social purposes to improve teaching strategy and learning performance in higher educational organizations. The outcomes of this research would support the evolution of M-learning at the university-level and cause shifting the traditional learning methods by merging M-learning methodologies as a learning management system that provides mobile learning services to students and teachers any time and from any location. result.paraphrase: Recently, mobile technology has been viewed as an effective means of improving students’ skills such as positive thinking, collaboration, and communication, and as a key element of major innovation across many e-learning research areas. Driven by 21st-century requirements, skills have been developed to meet the growing needs of higher education, leading to a paradigm shift from traditional teaching methods to M-learning. In this study, we examine the impact of mobile learning techniques on improving learning outcomes in higher education. A web-based survey was carried out using two questionnaires distributed to 200 second- and third-level students in the Computer Science Department at both the Community College and the College of Arts and Science. The study investigates e-learning through mobile technology to identify students’ perceptions of accepting mobile techniques and to assess the quality of mobile services for academic and social purposes, with the aim of improving teaching strategies and learning performance in higher-education institutions. The findings support the development of M-learning at university level and encourage a shift away from traditional learning methods by integrating M-learning methodologies into a learning management system that offers mobile learning services to students and teachers anytime and anywhere. The study highlights several important results for integrating mobile technology into teaching, including positive student perception, improved student concentration, flexible access to m-services for learning materials, and enhanced students’ skills in using mobile technology for e-learning.
